title: task complete succeeds with unchecked acceptance criteria / definition of done -- undocumented, likely intended, needs a durable line
description:
Reported inbound by quest-web via the orchestrator: created a task with an unchecked acceptance criterion, ran task complete, and it succeeded with the AC still checked: false -- no block, no warning, no diagnostic. The orchestrator asked for a ruling (defect, intended, or enforcement on an unexercised path) before questgraph.dev's public copy asserts anything about gate enforcement.

Established by direct source investigation, not inference from behavior alone:

1. Zero enforcement exists anywhere in src/ tying acceptanceCriteria or definitionOfDone (same shape, same question, DoD wasn't separately tested by quest-web but shares the identical code path) to a completion/transition check. Confirmed by reading TasksService.complete() (tasks.ts ~635) and the domain transitionTask() (domain/tasks/tasks.ts ~437) line by line, plus an exhaustive grep for '.checked' across src/ -- every hit is schema validation of the checked:boolean type or migration pass-through, never a completion gate.

2. transitionTask() DOES gate the terminal transition on something: blockingGatesSatisfied(...) over the task's gates/gateEvents -- a structurally SEPARATE field from acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone. This is reading (3) from the report, but it applies only to gates, not to acceptance criteria -- see the companion task filed alongside this one, because gates itself turns out to have no CLI write path (same shape as QCLI-251).

3. My ruling: most likely INTENDED (reading 2), not a defect -- but this is an inference from adjacent philosophy text, not a confirmed engineering decision, and I'm saying so plainly rather than overclaiming certainty. This project's own task-finalization agent-instructions (quest instructions task-finalization) already state the philosophy explicitly: 'An acceptance criterion you cannot prove stays unchecked, and the reason belongs in the notes... A criterion checked on faith is worse than one left open, because it stops anyone else from looking.' That describes and endorses closing a task with an honestly-unchecked criterion -- the tool's role is to record truthfully what was proven, not to force a closer to lie about completeness by ticking boxes to get past a gate. No ADR, spec, or code comment establishes this as a deliberate CLI-enforcement decision, though -- it is absent by omission, not by a documented choice.

4. The gap the orchestrator flagged either way: quest task complete --help (command-help.ts) says only 'Move a task to its terminal complete status' -- nothing about acceptance criteria being advisory. The natural assumption on seeing an acceptance-criteria field with a checked flag is that something enforces it before closure; nothing here corrects that assumption anywhere a caller would actually look.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A design decision is confirmed (not just inferred): acceptance criteria and definition-of-done stay advisory at completion by design, or quest task complete should refuse/warn on unchecked items -- record which, and why, durably (an ADR or a spec note, not just a task record)

quest task complete --help and command-help.ts state plainly whether unchecked acceptance criteria/definition-of-done block completion, so the natural assumption someone forms from seeing the field is corrected at the point they would look

If advisory is confirmed as the decision: task view / task list --json surfaces unchecked-criteria-at-completion as a visible signal (e.g. in the completed record, or in doctor/overview) rather than only in the raw checked:false state someone has to know to look for

If enforcement is decided instead: quest task complete gains a way to refuse or require an explicit override (e.g. --force) when acceptance criteria or definition-of-done remain unchecked, matching the existing blocking-gate pattern in transitionTask

plan: 1. Decide: acceptance criteria/DoD stay advisory (non-blocking) at completion -- consistent with task-finalization philosophy already in this repo (an honestly-unchecked criterion beats one checked on faith) -- but completion must stop being silent about it.

2. Update TasksService.complete() completion envelope to include an additive field reporting unresolved acceptance-criteria/DoD items (index+text) when any remain unchecked; omit when none (matches existing omit-when-undefined rendering convention).
3. Update --plain rendering to print a visible warning listing the unresolved items when present.
4. Correct command-help.ts task complete help text to state plainly that unchecked items do not block completion and are reported, not silently dropped.

5. Record the decision durably via quest decision create, referencing this task and the two live incidents (quest-web report that opened this task; a second fleet session closing two tasks with 0/3 criteria checked on 2026-09-13).
6. Add/extend an integration test: completion still exits 0 with unchecked items, envelope carries the new field, --plain prints the warning.
7. Two-pass consumer sweep (CLAUDE.md) since this is an additive envelope-shape change: grep the bare field name and grep the task complete invocation across sibling repos.
8. Branch, PR into dev, land; promote to main separately per normal cadence.
implementationNotes: Second live incident, relayed by the orchestrator 2026-09-13: another fleet session closed two tasks with 0 of 3 acceptance criteria checked, via the older 1-based --check-ac trap (QCLI-269) whose usage errors were piped to /dev/null and went unseen. What makes this occurrence load-bearing for the fix: every other known quest flag trap is a write that FAILS quietly (catchable by re-reading the record); this is a write that SUCCEEDS with a wrong-looking record and nothing about the completion result says so. Reinforces AC1/AC2 (surface the gap, do not just document it) -- proceeding with advisory-but-loud rather than hard enforcement, since OFLE-19 (opum-fleet) already has a legitimate deferred-criterion close (a post-merge fact) that a hard block would have obstructed.
finalSummary: Decided (DEC-1): acceptance criteria / definition-of-done stay advisory at task complete -- consistent with this project's own task-finalization philosophy (an honestly-unchecked item beats one checked on faith) and with a real legitimate deferred-criterion close (opum-fleet's OFLE-19). What changed is visibility, not enforcement: quest task complete now computes an additive unresolvedAtCompletion field on its JSON result (acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone unchecked items by index+text, present only when non-empty) and prints a stderr line prefixed 'Warning:' naming them -- exit code and the completed record's existing fields are untouched. command-help.ts's task complete summary and the task-finalization agent guide now state this plainly (AC1). Verified: bun run check (typecheck, lint, format, layer:check, full suite) exits 0, 460/460 tests pass including 4 new ones in test/qcli252-completion-visibility.test.ts covering the unresolved-items case, the fully-checked case (field absent, stderr silent), --plain rendering, and that edit/view never carry the field. Two-pass consumer sweep run against sibling checkouts under /Volumes/external/repos: pass 1 (bare field grep) found no existing reader of the new unresolvedAtCompletion key, since it is brand new -- nothing to break. Pass 2 (invocation grep, 'task','complete') found opum-cli-e2e's suites/45-parity-backlog.mjs and 21-quest-records.mjs driving quest task complete; both check via check.successEnvelope, which validates only the outer {schemaVersion,kind,data,principal} shape and that data is an object -- it does not enumerate data's keys, so the additive field is invisible to it. No test anywhere calls check.stderrSilentOnSuccess with allowWarnings:false against task complete; the contract's own default already tolerates a 'warning'-prefixed stderr line on success. AC3 ('if enforcement is decided instead...') is deliberately left unchecked: enforcement was not the decision, so nothing was built against it, and checking it would misrepresent what happened -- DEC-1 records the reasoning for future reference.
